summary: crypto-javas exfiltrates process.env and CI metadata on install and import
details: crypto-javas@2.0.8 is a credential-harvesting package disguised as a 'Lightweight utility library'. Its package.json declares a postinstall hook (`node setup.js`) that runs on `npm install`, and its main entry (`index.js`) invokes an `autoExecute()` routine at module top level, so the same behavior also fires on `require`/`import`. Both paths enumerate `process.env`, filter out only a small set of shell-shape variables (PATH, HOME, USER, etc.), and POST the entire remaining environment together with CI identifiers (GITHUB_RUN_ID, CI_JOB_ID, commit SHA, branch, repository) as JSON to an HTTPS endpoint (`BACKEND_URL`) with an `X-API-Key` header, both loaded from environment variables or a `.crypto-config.json`/`package.json` config. Publisher metadata is empty (`author: ""`, `repository.url: ""`) and the package name/description do not correspond to the actual behavior. In a CI build the harvested set typically includes NPM_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS_*, cloud provider secrets, and other build credentials.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
